parsed.explanation: The combined national and state regime is actively hostile. National binary-sex passport and entry policy can refuse or tag cases involving document discrepancy, with fraud and lifetime-ineligibility risk; state law mandates birth-sex facilities, shelter and prison placement, treats identity-congruent bathroom use as indecent exposure, bans minor care, and criminalises gender-expressive performance. Detention carries documented abuse. National hate-crime and employment protections exist, but state enforcement and recourse are thin; the 7.8/100k violence figure is an admitted undercount floor and cannot establish a rate. A visitor is not routinely arrested for mere discovery and no death penalty applies, so this sits above the 0.15 tier, but documented criminal, facility and custody exposures place it well below administrative-friction anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary-sex rule; X markers no longer issued; entry refusal where documents or records cast doubt on sex; possible material-misrepresentation and lifetime ineligibility; athlete ban. Visitor uses a home passport, but border officers apply these checks.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; passport policy is in litigation; legal-aid FAQ exists. No operative visitor remedy at the border is documented.
entry_documents.interaction: A document or presentation mismatch can trigger secondary inspection and fraud referral, moving from travel friction to exclusion or removal.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody is documented with forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of trans men; national corrections use conversion-style practices; state prisons place by birth sex and ban inmate care.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some national executive orders have been enjoined; no visitor-specific custody protection is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border discrepancy can lead to detention, then birth-sex custody or immigration custody with severe harm.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: The state's 2026 Act requires birth-sex facilities and bars trans women from shelters; a 2019 statute defines identity-congruent bathroom use as indecent exposure; prisons are birth-sex segregated; many national and state facility bans exist.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No operative exemption for trans visitors is documented; national injunctions cited are unrelated to these state facility rules.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Any public building, shelter, hospital or police custody can force birth-sex placement and possible criminal exposure.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care for minors, via telehealth, and for inmates; civil penalties and regret suits apply; national insurance restrictions are proposed. Adult routine care is not explicitly banned, but the climate is hostile.
care_services.protection: National litigation has blocked some orders; no protection for this state's care ban or for trans visitors is documented.
care_services.interaction: Travelling with a trans minor or seeking care can create legal risk for providers and families; adult emergency care may force disclosure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups; a justice reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; the state has a drag ban, school outing rules, no gender-identity hate-crime statute, and reports of police indifference.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime law covers gender identity; a state prosecutor opinion allows gender-based enhancement; some national orders are enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Presentation or advocacy can draw scrutiny; state police response to anti-trans violence is unreliable.

minors_guardians.exposure: The state care ban is upheld; laws penalise helpers; schools must out name or pronoun requests; sports and facilities are birth-sex restricted; national guidance threatens teachers; parent regret suits are authorised.
minors_guardians.protection: Some national orders are enjoined and litigation is ongoing; no state protection for trans minors or their guardians is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor faces care and reporting exposure; a trans child in school may be outed to guardians or investigated.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented discrimination, refusal of service and beatings; police and legal officials reported turning a blind eye; gay and trans panic defence remains available; state hate-crime law omits gender identity. The 7.8/100k figure is an admitted undercount floor, so it cannot establish a rate.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime law and a prosecutor opinion provide theoretical enhancement; no state gender-identity hate-crime coverage is documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A visitor is isolated; reporting may not produce investigation, and the panic defence reduces deterrence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statewide nondiscrimination law; municipal protections are preempted; the licence-marker suit outcome is unknown; enforcement of the 2019 indecent-exposure and 2026 facility, shelter and prison provisions is not documented; drag-ban litigation continues.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National employment ruling, marriage recognition, civil-liberties litigation and a legal-aid FAQ exist; remedies are slow and contested.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: A short-stay visitor has little realistic recourse; unresolved enforcement increases uncertainty but does not neutralise documented restrictions.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.15-A has routine arrests for presentation, months of pretrial custody, beatings, and an available capital pathway. This dossier lacks routine visitor arrests for mere presentation and any capital exposure, but shares severe custody harm and hostile law; it sits above 0.15-A.

0.35-A is administrative exclusion and humiliation by a border register without arrest. Here exposure includes criminal facility and performance laws, possible fraud-based exclusion, and documented abusive custody, so this jurisdiction is lower than 0.35-A.

0.55-B involves secondary screening and refused admission, mostly administrative, with an appeal desk. This jurisdiction adds birth-sex facilities, criminal exposure and severe detention conditions; it is clearly below 0.55-B.
0.75-C has trained border officers, tribunal appeals, brief detention and no credible imprisonment. This dossier has active hostile statutes and custody abuse, far below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces a layered regime: national border policy can turn a document or presentation mismatch into refusal, secondary inspection or a fraud finding; state law then mandates birth-sex facilities, shelters and prisons, criminalises some gender-expressive performance and identity-congruent bathroom use, and bans minor care. Detention is the highest-severity pathway, with documented abusive custody. National hate-crime and employment protections and ongoing litigation are real but partial, and state-level recourse is thin. Because routine visitor arrests for mere discovery and capital punishment are not documented, the rating stays above the 0.15 tier, but the documented criminal, facility, care and custody exposures keep it in the high-risk band.
